Preserve these established identities, mature adult proportions, watercolor/ink-on-paper texture, muted indigo and warm ochre, bedside lamp, wooden couch, ivory bedding and tent; deliberately recompose the actors so BOTH faces and their mutual eyelines are legible.
Exact literary instant: chapter49 first sickbed conversation, immediately after Kongming smilingly alludes to unpredictable wind and Zhou Yu loses color and masks his alarm with a groan. BEFORE the written prescription, before the offer of southeast wind, before any assassination decision.
Two opposing subjective positions: Kongming knows the strategic anxiety but speaks in courteous medical euphemism, gently testing whether Zhou Yu recognizes the hint. Zhou Yu needs this ally's help yet protects his authority and his unspoken concern; a startled involuntary reaction breaks through his formal composure. Do not portray either as an evil villain.
Composition: eye-level intimate TWO-SHOT at an oblique angle, both faces similarly large in readable three-quarter views, Kongming left, supported seated Zhou Yu right. Do NOT conceal Kongming behind a big back/shoulder. No one looks at viewer. Their eyes meet across a narrow gap; bedding and couch separate their bodies without separating the conversation.
Act Kongming: relaxed upright seated posture, steady attentive eyes on Zhou Yu, gently lifted mouth corners and a restrained knowing smile rather than a grin, brows relaxed, one open hand resting quietly near his own knee, no diagnosing touch and no pointed finger. He quietly controls the pace by waiting.
Act Zhou Yu: pale fatigued face, inner brows tighten and eyelids widen subtly at the allusion, eyes remain searching Kongming's face, parted lips in a restrained exhalation/groan as he attempts to recover composure, jaw held. One hand bunches a small fold of the ivory coverlet near his abdomen, a physical leak of anxiety; shoulders subtly tense while he remains supported seated, not leaping up. His face should convey alert defensive intelligence and momentary exposure, not generic anger, blank handsomeness or severe medical distress.
Faces are the sharpest focal detail, hands secondary, soft tent behind. Shared natural warm lamplight with soft indigo shadow, no good-versus-evil split lighting. Keep faces and hands inside frame, not a poster or sprite collage. edits.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story / identity-preserve scene revision.
Asset: finished opaque 16:9 landscape narrative painting for an illustrated Chinese novel reader.
Input image1 is the EDIT TARGET, existing Huarong encounter. Image2 is Cao Cao identity reference (mature broad face, arched heavy brows, dark moustache and medium beard with grey, charcoal robe with dull bronze trim); image3 is Guan Yu identity reference (naturally ruddy face, straight brows, long black beard, green headcloth and green robe over dark lamellar armor). Preserve identity, ink/watercolor grain, muted indigo/umber palette, cold wet bamboo pass, exhausted northern army, small disciplined southern guard, two mounted men, tired dark horse for Cao and chestnut-red horse for Guan. Recompose for much clearer facial acting and opposing motivations.
Exact literary instant: chapter50 paragraph beginning Cao approaches Guan and bows from horseback, during his appeal to their former relationship and Guan's reply that military duty cannot be set aside for private feeling. BEFORE Guan turns his horse, opens the line or allows anyone to pass. No one has been released.
Cao's position: badly outmatched and exhausted, he chooses a personal appeal as his remaining tactic. Humility is deliberate, fear and calculation coexist. Guan's position: controls the road and is bound by a military pledge; formally refuses the appeal, while old obligation is being invoked. His compassion and eventual choice must NOT already be resolved. This is a difficult negotiation, not two friends greeting and not villain versus saint.
Composition: medium-wide oblique side TWO-SHOT, Cao left and Guan right, both mounted and both faces large enough to read in three-quarter view. Crop lower horses naturally below the chest if necessary to prioritize faces and hands; no huge foreground back obscuring Cao's face. Their heads are at comparable human scale, Guan slightly more upright, empty narrow road gap between them. No one looks at viewer.
Cao acting: upper body bows slightly forward while staying in saddle, chin lowered but eyes lifted toward Guan to search for a response, tired creases under eyes, knitted inner brows, mouth slightly open mid courteous appeal with restrained strained softness, NOT a knowing smirk or comic grin. One hand stays on reins, other performs a modest controlled greeting at chest height. Mud-spattered robe and fatigue, but no theatrical kneeling or begging hands raised overhead.
Guan acting: squared shoulders and upright torso deliberately maintain the barrier, chin level, lips firmly closed following his formal answer, brow subtly drawn, direct guarded gaze toward Cao; restrained tension near eyes and jaw suggests the personal cost of holding duty, NOT furious shouting, sentimental smile, downward vacant gaze or a visibly merciful decision. One hand holds reins close and still; other holds a single guandao shaft vertical, its blade above and safely away from people, not attacking and not lowering/opening the route.
Groups embody different stakes: behind Cao, a few weary damp soldiers lean on each other or watch Guan with anxious expectant faces; one grips his reins tightly. Behind Guan, several sentries remain upright, ordered and alert, watching their commander and keeping the road closed. No copied identical faces or poses. Main pair dominates; crowd is secondary and small, not extra famous named characters.
Cold diffuse daylight shared by both sides, subtle warm skin tones without divine halo. Human psychological tension, realistic anatomy. No palace, camp buildings, inscriptions on banners, text, captions, watermark, modern objects, gore, combat, release procession or later turning-horse action. Literary artistic interpretation.
